data.name: Jiyad
data.gender_notes: Jiyad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'jihad', meaning to strive, struggle, or exert effort. In Islamic context, it refers to the internal and external struggle to uphold faith and good deeds. The name Jiyad carries the meaning “Struggle, Striving, Jihad” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jiyad usually hope their child will grow to embody struggle, striving, jihad and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to remain steadfast in faith and persevere through challenges.
data.etymology: Jiyad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Struggle, Striving, Jihad.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jiyad total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: جِيَاد
in_arabic.long_meaning: جِيَاد هو اسم علم من أسماء الله الحسنى، ويُشير إلى الجيادية في الصبر والصبر، وهو اسم مشتق من الجود، والجود هو أحد أسماء الله الحسنى، ويُشير إلى الجود وال سخاء، ويُستخدم اسم جِيَاد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الزمر، آية 9، ويُشير إلى جود الله وتكافؤه، ويُعد جِيَاد اسمًا حسنًا، يُستخدم في تسمية الأطفال، ويمثل الجود والصبر والصبر في الإسلام.

in_urdu.name: جیاد
in_urdu.long_meaning: جیاد ایک بچوں کا نام ہے، جو اسلامی اعتقادات کے مطابق جِیادی صبر اور سخاوت کے معنی میں ہے۔ یہ نام اسلام کی شہادت کے ناموں میں سے ایک ہے اور یہ نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اسلامی روایت کے مطابق جِیاد نام جود اور سخاوت کے معنی میں ہے۔

In Islamic tradition, Jiyad is considered a name that represents the qualities of perseverance, virtue, and guardianship. It is a name that is deeply rooted in Arabic culture and is often given to children born into Muslim families. Jiyad is also considered a name that reflects the Islamic values of patience, perseverance, and self-control.
